name: TMS9900 (TI-99/4A, xas99)
about: The 16-bit chip inside the TI-99/4A. Written for the xas99 assembler.

caseFormat._about: Which letter case each part is changed to when you save (or press Shift+Alt+U): upper, lower or keep (leave as typed). Numbers, comments and text in quotes are never changed.

lineUp._about: Where each part of a line starts when you line up the code (Shift+Alt+L), counting from 0: the instruction, the operands and an end-of-line comment. A label always starts in column 0. commentGap is the fewest spaces kept before a comment when the code is too long to reach the comment column. You can change these here, or for one chip in the retroAsm.lineUpColumns setting.

build._about: How to build and run code for this chip. xas99 is run by the extension itself (it also makes the disc image with xdm99), so there is no command here. Classic99 is started after a build.

tool.name: xas99
tool.why: turns TI-99/4A source into a program
tool.get: Download the newest xdt99-<version>-Windows.zip (or the .zip for Mac and Linux) from the Releases page and unzip it into your tools folder. It also needs Python 3.

run.name: Classic99
run.why: pretends to be a TI-99/4A (Windows only)
run.get: Download Classic99 from its website and unzip it into your tools folder. It runs on Windows only; on Mac or Linux use another emulator (such as MAME) and set retroAsm.build.runCommand.

debug.name: MAME
debug.why: runs a real TI-99/4A so you can stop and step through your program
debug.get: Download MAME from mamedev.org and unpack it into its own folder (inside your tools folder is fine). It also needs the TI-99/4A system ROMs as ti99_4a.zip in a folder called roms beside mame.exe.

sizing.loadNote: Editor/Assembler puts a program like this at >A000, the start of the 24K part of the 32K memory expansion

registers.about: A register is one of 16 words of ordinary memory, starting wherever LWPI pointed. Byte instructions (MOVB, AB, CB ...) use only its left byte.

notes.R0: Special: can't be used as the index in @LABEL(R0). A shift with a count of 0 takes its count from R0.
notes.R11: Special: BL puts the way back here. B *R11 (or RT) returns. A routine that uses BL itself must save R11 first.
notes.R12: Special: the CRU base. SBO, SBZ, TB, LDCR and STCR all count from the hardware line R12 points at.
notes.R13: Special: BLWP saves the old register position (workspace pointer) here. RTWP puts it back.
notes.R14: Special: BLWP saves the old program position here. RTWP puts it back.
notes.R15: Special: BLWP saves the old status flags here. RTWP puts them back.

operandForms.text: the {unit} {r1} points at ({1} then moves on by {step})
operandForms.name: Register points at memory, then moves on
operandForms.help: The register holds an address. The instruction uses the memory at that address, then adds 1 (byte instructions) or 2 (word instructions) to the register so it points at the next one. Handy for walking through a list.

operandForms.name: Register points at memory
operandForms.help: The register holds an address. The instruction uses the memory at that address, not the register itself.

operandForms.name: Register points at memory, plus an offset
operandForms.help: The register holds an address. The number in front is added to it (the register itself is not changed) and the instruction uses the memory there. R0 can't be used this way.

operandForms.name: Table lookup
operandForms.help: The address is the label plus whatever is in the register (the register is not changed). Used to pick one entry out of a table. R0 can't be used this way.

operandForms.name: Memory at a fixed address
operandForms.help: The @ means "the memory at this address". Without the @ you would get the address number itself.

timing._about: How long each instruction takes. "cycles" is the clock cycles and "access" how many times it reads or writes memory, both before the operands ([if not, if so] for jumps; "cyclesByCount" when it depends on a count); "operandCost" adds the cycles and memory uses for each way of writing a general operand. Numbers from the TMS9900 data manual.
timing.about: The TI-99/4A's TMS9900 runs at 3 million cycles a second. The console ROM (>0000 to >1FFF) and the 256 bytes of RAM at >8300 are fast; everything else (the 32K expansion, cartridges, the video, sound and speech chips) is slow, and each read or write there adds 4 cycles. So code in the 32K expansion with its registers at >8300 runs somewhere between the two numbers in the tooltip.
timing.pair: {1} cycles if it doesn't jump, {2} if it does
timing.accessText: plus up to {extra} more in slow memory (it reads or writes memory {times}; each slow one adds {slow})

MOV.name: Move word
MOV.summary: Copies a word (2 bytes) from one place to another. The source is not changed.
MOV.more: It also compares the copied value with 0, so `MOV R6,R6` is a common trick to ask "is R6 zero?" before a JEQ or JNE.
MOV.flags: Result flags (compared with 0): JEQ, JNE, JGT, JLT can follow.

special.text: Test {1}: copying it onto itself changes nothing, but sets the flags so the next jump can ask "is it zero?"

MOVB.name: Move byte
MOVB.summary: Copies one byte from one place to another. With a register, it is the left byte that is used; the right byte is left alone.
MOVB.more: It also compares the copied byte with 0, so a JEQ or JNE can follow straight away.
MOVB.flags: Result flags (compared with 0): JEQ, JNE, JGT, JLT can follow.

SWPB.name: Swap bytes
SWPB.summary: Swaps the left and right bytes of a word. Used a lot because byte instructions only reach the left byte of a register.
SWPB.explain: Swap the left and right bytes of {1}.

LI.name: Load immediate
LI.summary: Puts a number (or the address of a label) straight into a register.
LI.more: To set the left byte, put the value in the top two hex digits: `LI R1,>0500` makes the left byte 5.

SETO.name: Set to ones
SETO.summary: Sets every bit of a word to 1. That is >FFFF, which also means -1.

LWPI.name: Load workspace pointer
LWPI.summary: Chooses where in memory the 16 registers live. R0 is at that address, R1 two bytes later, and so on (32 bytes in all).

STWP.name: Store workspace pointer
STWP.summary: Puts the address where the registers currently live into a register.
STWP.explain: Put the address of the registers into {1}.

STST.name: Store status
STST.summary: Copies the status flags (equal, greater, carry and so on) into a register.

A.name: Add words
A.summary: Adds the source to the destination. The answer goes in the destination.
A.flags: Result flags, plus carry and overflow.

AB.name: Add bytes
AB.summary: Adds one byte to another. The answer goes in the destination byte. With a register, it is the left byte.
AB.flags: Result flags, plus carry and overflow.

AI.name: Add immediate
AI.summary: Adds a number to a register. There is no "subtract immediate": add a negative number instead (`AI R1,-10`).
AI.more: To add to the left byte only, put the number in the top two hex digits: `AI R1,>0100` adds 1 to the left byte.
AI.flags: Result flags, plus carry and overflow.

S.name: Subtract words
S.summary: Takes the source away from the destination. The answer goes in the destination.
S.flags: Result flags, plus carry and overflow.

SB.name: Subtract bytes
SB.summary: Takes one byte away from another. The answer goes in the destination byte.
SB.flags: Result flags, plus carry and overflow.

INC.name: Increment
INC.flags: Result flags, plus carry and overflow.

INCT.name: Increment by two
INCT.summary: Adds 2. Useful for stepping a pointer on to the next word.
INCT.flags: Result flags, plus carry and overflow.

DEC.name: Decrement
DEC.summary: Takes 1 away. Often followed by JNE to make a loop that counts down to 0.
DEC.flags: Result flags, plus carry and overflow.

DECT.name: Decrement by two
DECT.flags: Result flags, plus carry and overflow.

NEG.name: Negate
NEG.flags: Result flags, plus carry and overflow.
NEG.explain: Flip the sign of {1} (plus becomes minus, minus becomes plus).

ABS.cyclesPair: {1} cycles if the number is already positive, {2} if not
ABS.name: Absolute value
ABS.summary: Makes a negative number positive. A positive number is left alone.
ABS.flags: Result flags, set from the value before it was changed.
ABS.explain: Make {1} positive if it was negative.

MPY.name: Multiply
MPY.summary: Multiplies the register by the source (both treated as unsigned). The answer is 32 bits, so it fills two registers: the top half in the register you named, the bottom half in the next one.
MPY.more: For small numbers the whole answer is in the next register. `MPY R0,R1` leaves it in R2.
MPY.explain: Multiply {2} by {1}. The answer is 32 bits: top half in {2}, bottom half in {next2}.

DIV.cyclesPair: {2} to {3} cycles, or {1} if the answer is too big to fit
DIV.name: Divide
DIV.summary: Divides a 32-bit number (top half in the register you named, bottom half in the next one) by the source. The answer goes in the named register and the remainder in the next one.
DIV.more: Clear the top-half register first if your number fits in 16 bits. If the answer would not fit, nothing changes and the overflow flag is set.
DIV.flags: Overflow only (set when the answer would not fit).
DIV.explain: Divide the 32-bit number in {2} and {next2} by {1}. Answer in {2}, remainder in {next2}.

C.name: Compare words
C.summary: Compares two words. Nothing is changed; only the flags are set, ready for a jump.
C.more: After `C A,B`: JEQ if A = B, JNE if not. Unsigned: JH if A > B, JHE if A >= B, JL if A < B, JLE if A <= B. Signed: JGT if A > B, JLT if A < B.
C.explain: Compare {1} with {2}. Nothing changes; the next jump decides.

CB.name: Compare bytes
CB.summary: Compares two bytes. Nothing is changed; only the flags are set, ready for a jump.
CB.more: After `CB A,B`: JEQ if A = B, JNE if not. Unsigned: JH if A > B, JHE if A >= B, JL if A < B, JLE if A <= B. Signed: JGT if A > B, JLT if A < B.
CB.explain: Compare {1} with {2}. Nothing changes; the next jump decides.

CI.name: Compare immediate
CI.summary: Compares a register with a number. Nothing is changed; only the flags are set, ready for a jump.
CI.more: After `CI R1,10`: JEQ if R1 = 10, JNE if not. Unsigned: JH if R1 > 10, JHE if >=, JL if <, JLE if <=. Signed: JGT if R1 > 10, JLT if R1 < 10.
CI.explain: Compare {1} with {2}. Nothing changes; the next jump decides.

COC.name: Compare ones
COC.summary: Asks: are all the bits that are 1 in the mask also 1 in the register? JEQ means yes, JNE means no. Nothing is changed.
COC.explain: Are all the 1 bits of {1} also on in {2}? (JEQ = yes, JNE = no)

CZC.name: Compare zeros
CZC.summary: Asks: are all the bits that are 1 in the mask 0 in the register? JEQ means yes, JNE means no. Nothing is changed.
CZC.explain: Are all the 1 bits of {1} off in {2}? (JEQ = yes, JNE = no)

ANDI.name: AND immediate
ANDI.summary: Keeps only the bits of the register that are also 1 in the mask. Every other bit becomes 0.
ANDI.more: Used to pick out part of a number: `ANDI R1,7` keeps the bottom 3 bits (the leftover after dividing by 8).
ANDI.explain: Keep only the bits of {1} that are 1 in {2}; the rest become 0.

ORI.name: OR immediate
ORI.summary: Switches on, in the register, every bit that is 1 in the mask. Other bits are left alone.
ORI.explain: Switch on in {1} the bits that are 1 in {2}.

XOR.name: Exclusive OR
XOR.summary: Flips, in the register, every bit that is 1 in the source. Other bits are left alone.
XOR.explain: Flip in {2} every bit that is 1 in {1}.

INV.name: Invert
INV.summary: Flips every bit: each 0 becomes 1 and each 1 becomes 0.

SOC.name: Set ones corresponding (OR)
SOC.summary: Switches on, in the destination, every bit that is 1 in the source. This is the chip's OR.
SOC.explain: Switch on in {2} every bit that is 1 in {1}.

SOCB.name: Set ones corresponding, byte (OR)
SOCB.summary: Switches on, in the destination byte, every bit that is 1 in the source byte.
SOCB.explain: Switch on in {2} every bit that is 1 in {1}.

SZC.name: Set zeros corresponding
SZC.summary: Switches off, in the destination, every bit that is 1 in the source. (The chip has no plain AND between two places; this is the nearest thing.)
SZC.explain: Switch off in {2} every bit that is 1 in {1}.

SZCB.name: Set zeros corresponding, byte
SZCB.summary: Switches off, in the destination byte, every bit that is 1 in the source byte.
SZCB.explain: Switch off in {2} every bit that is 1 in {1}.

cyclesByCount.zero: 20 cycles, plus 2 for each place it moves (the count comes from R0)
cyclesByCount.unknown: 12 cycles, plus 2 for each place it moves

SLA.name: Shift left
SLA.summary: Slides all the bits to the left. Each place doubles the number. Zeros come in on the right.
SLA.more: A count of 0 means "use the count held in R0".
SLA.flags: Result flags, plus carry (the last bit pushed out) and overflow.
SLA.explain: Shift {1} left by {2} (the same as multiplying by {pow2}).

cyclesByCount.zero: 20 cycles, plus 2 for each place it moves (the count comes from R0)
cyclesByCount.unknown: 12 cycles, plus 2 for each place it moves

SRL.name: Shift right (logical)
SRL.summary: Slides all the bits to the right. Each place halves the number. Zeros come in on the left, so use it for unsigned numbers.
SRL.more: `SRL R1,8` moves the left byte down into the right byte. A count of 0 means "use the count held in R0".
SRL.flags: Result flags, plus carry (the last bit pushed out).
SRL.explain: Shift {1} right by {2} (the same as dividing by {pow2}).

cyclesByCount.zero: 20 cycles, plus 2 for each place it moves (the count comes from R0)
cyclesByCount.unknown: 12 cycles, plus 2 for each place it moves

SRA.name: Shift right (arithmetic)
SRA.summary: Slides all the bits to the right, but keeps the sign: a negative number stays negative. Use it to halve signed numbers.
SRA.more: A count of 0 means "use the count held in R0".
SRA.flags: Result flags, plus carry (the last bit pushed out).
SRA.explain: Shift {1} right by {2}, keeping its sign (the same as dividing by {pow2}).
SRA.explainNoPow: Shift {1} right by {2}, keeping its sign.

cyclesByCount.zero: 20 cycles, plus 2 for each place it moves (the count comes from R0)
cyclesByCount.unknown: 12 cycles, plus 2 for each place it moves

SRC.name: Shift right circular (rotate)
SRC.summary: Slides all the bits to the right. Bits that fall off the right end come back in on the left, so nothing is lost.
SRC.more: `SRC R1,8` swaps the two bytes. A count of 0 means "use the count held in R0".
SRC.flags: Result flags, plus carry (the last bit moved round).
SRC.explain: Rotate {1} right by {2} (bits that fall off the right come back in on the left).

JMP.name: Jump
JMP.summary: Always jumps to the label. Short range only: about 127 instructions forwards or back. For further, use B @label.

JEQ.name: Jump if equal
JEQ.summary: Jumps if the last result was 0, or the two things just compared were equal. Otherwise carries on with the next line.
JEQ.explain: Jump to {1} if the last result was 0 (or the two things compared were equal).

JNE.name: Jump if not equal
JNE.summary: Jumps if the last result was not 0, or the two things just compared were different. Otherwise carries on with the next line.
JNE.explain: Jump to {1} if the last result was not 0 (or the two things compared were different).

JGT.name: Jump if greater than (signed)
JGT.summary: Jumps if the first thing compared was greater than the second, treating both as signed numbers (so -1 is less than 1). After an ordinary instruction: jumps if the result was above 0.
JGT.explain: Jump to {1} if the first was greater than the second, signed (or the last result was above 0).

JLT.name: Jump if less than (signed)
JLT.summary: Jumps if the first thing compared was less than the second, treating both as signed numbers. After an ordinary instruction: jumps if the result was below 0.
JLT.explain: Jump to {1} if the first was less than the second, signed (or the last result was below 0).

JH.name: Jump if high (unsigned)
JH.summary: Jumps if the first thing compared was greater than the second, treating both as unsigned numbers (so >FFFF is the biggest, not -1).
JH.explain: Jump to {1} if the first was greater than the second (unsigned).

JHE.name: Jump if high or equal (unsigned)
JHE.summary: Jumps if the first thing compared was greater than or equal to the second, treating both as unsigned numbers.
JHE.explain: Jump to {1} if the first was greater than or equal to the second (unsigned).

JL.name: Jump if low (unsigned)
JL.summary: Jumps if the first thing compared was less than the second, treating both as unsigned numbers.
JL.explain: Jump to {1} if the first was less than the second (unsigned).

JLE.name: Jump if low or equal (unsigned)
JLE.summary: Jumps if the first thing compared was less than or equal to the second, treating both as unsigned numbers.
JLE.explain: Jump to {1} if the first was less than or equal to the second (unsigned).

JOC.name: Jump on carry
JOC.summary: Jumps if the carry flag is on. After a shift, carry holds the last bit that was pushed out, so this asks "was that bit a 1?". After an add, carry means the answer was too big to fit.
JOC.explain: Jump to {1} if the carry flag is on (for example, the bit just shifted out was 1).

JNC.name: Jump if no carry
JNC.summary: Jumps if the carry flag is off. After a shift: the last bit pushed out was 0.
JNC.explain: Jump to {1} if the carry flag is off.

JNO.name: Jump if no overflow
JNO.summary: Jumps if the overflow flag is off (the last signed sum fitted properly).
JNO.explain: Jump to {1} if there was no overflow.

JOP.name: Jump on odd parity
JOP.summary: Jumps if the last byte handled had an odd number of 1 bits. Rarely needed.
JOP.explain: Jump to {1} if the last byte had an odd number of 1 bits.

B.name: Branch
B.summary: Jumps to any address, however far away. No way back is saved. `B *R11` is the usual way to return from a routine called with BL.
B.explain: Jump to {1t} (no way back is saved).

special.text: Return to the caller: jump to the address BL left in R11.

BL.name: Branch and link (call)
BL.summary: Calls a routine. The address of the next line is put in R11 first, so the routine can come back with `B *R11`.
BL.more: There is no stack. If a routine uses BL itself, R11 gets overwritten, so it has to save R11 somewhere first and get it back before returning.
BL.explain: Call the routine {1t}. The way back is put in R11.

BLWP.name: Branch and load workspace pointer
BLWP.summary: Calls a routine that has its own separate set of registers. The address you give holds two words: where the routine's registers live, and where its code starts. Your own registers are untouched while it runs.
BLWP.more: The old register position, program position and flags are saved in the new R13, R14 and R15. The routine returns with RTWP. The Editor/Assembler helpers (VSBW, VMBW, KSCAN ...) are called this way.
BLWP.explain: Call {1t}, which runs with its own set of registers and returns with RTWP.

special.text: Reset the console: back to the TI title screen.

RTWP.name: Return with workspace pointer
RTWP.summary: Returns from a routine called with BLWP (or from an interrupt). Puts back the caller's registers, position and flags from R13, R14 and R15.
RTWP.flags: All flags are put back to what the caller had.
RTWP.explain: Return from a BLWP call, putting the caller's registers and flags back.

RT.name: Return
RT.summary: Returns from a routine called with BL. It is just a shorter way of writing `B *R11`.
RT.explain: Return to the caller (the same as B *R11).

X.cyclesNote: plus the time of the instruction it runs, less 4
X.name: Execute
X.summary: Runs the single instruction stored at the source, as if it were written here. Rarely needed.
X.flags: Whatever the instruction it runs would change.
X.explain: Run the one instruction stored in {1}.

XOP.name: Extended operation
XOP.summary: Calls one of 16 special routines built into the system. Hardly used on the TI-99/4A.

SBO.name: Set bit to one
SBO.summary: Switches one hardware line on. The CRU is the chip's set of single-bit lines to things like the keyboard, joysticks and cassette. The number counts on from the line R12 points at.
SBO.explain: Switch on hardware line {1} (counted from the base in R12).

SBZ.name: Set bit to zero
SBZ.summary: Switches one hardware line off. The number counts on from the line R12 points at.
SBZ.explain: Switch off hardware line {1} (counted from the base in R12).

TB.name: Test bit
TB.summary: Reads one hardware line. JEQ then jumps if the line was 1, JNE if it was 0. The number counts on from the line R12 points at.
TB.flags: Equal flag only (on if the line was 1).
TB.explain: Read hardware line {1} (counted from the base in R12). JEQ = it was 1, JNE = it was 0.

LDCR.name: Load CRU (send bits out)
LDCR.summary: Sends several bits out to the hardware lines in one go, starting at the line R12 points at. With 8 bits or fewer, they come from the left byte of a register.
LDCR.more: On the TI-99/4A this is how you pick a keyboard column: R12 = >0024, then LDCR the column number with a count of 3.
LDCR.explain: Send {2} from {1} out to the hardware lines, starting at the base in R12.

cyclesByCount.unknown: 42 to 60 cycles, depending on how many bits

STCR.name: Store CRU (read bits in)
STCR.summary: Reads several bits in from the hardware lines in one go, starting at the line R12 points at. With 8 bits or fewer, they go into the left byte of a register.
STCR.more: On the TI-99/4A this is how you read the keyboard rows: R12 = >0006, then STCR with a count of 8. A pressed key reads as 0, which is why INV usually follows.
STCR.explain: Read {2} in from the hardware lines (starting at the base in R12) into {1}.

LIMI.name: Load interrupt mask
LIMI.summary: Turns interrupts on or off. `LIMI 0` = off: nothing can break into your code. `LIMI 2` = on: the console's own routine runs once per frame (sound lists, sprite motion, the QUIT key).

special.text: Turn interrupts off: nothing can break into the code from here on.
Turn interrupts on: the console's once-a-frame routine may run from here on.

NOP.name: No operation
NOP.summary: Does nothing, apart from taking a tiny amount of time. Used as a short pause.

IDLE.name: Idle
IDLE.summary: Stops and waits for an interrupt. Not normally used on the TI-99/4A.
IDLE.explain: Stop and wait for an interrupt.

RSET.name: Reset
RSET.summary: Sets the interrupt level to 0 and signals outside hardware. Not normally used on the TI-99/4A.
RSET.explain: Set the interrupt level to 0 and signal outside hardware.

CKON.name: Clock on
CKON.summary: Signals outside hardware. Does nothing useful on the TI-99/4A.
CKON.explain: Signal outside hardware (no use on the TI-99/4A).

CKOF.name: Clock off
CKOF.summary: Signals outside hardware. Does nothing useful on the TI-99/4A.
CKOF.explain: Signal outside hardware (no use on the TI-99/4A).

LREX.name: Load or restart execution
LREX.summary: Signals outside hardware. Does nothing useful on the TI-99/4A.
LREX.explain: Signal outside hardware (no use on the TI-99/4A).

EQU.name: Equate
EQU.summary: Gives a name to a number. It takes up no memory: wherever the name appears, the assembler swaps in the number.

WEQU.name: Weak equate (xas99)
WEQU.summary: Like EQU, but the name can be given a different value later without an error.

DATA.name: Word data
DATA.summary: Puts one or more words (2 bytes each) into the program at this point. Always starts on an even address.

BYTE.name: Byte data
BYTE.summary: Puts one or more single bytes into the program at this point. Follow a run of BYTEs with EVEN before any code or DATA.

TEXT.name: Text
TEXT.summary: Puts the letters of a piece of text into the program, one byte per letter.

STRI.name: Text with length (xas99)
STRI.summary: Like TEXT, but puts a byte holding the length of the text in front.

FLOA.name: Floating-point number (xas99)
FLOA.summary: Puts a number in the TI's 8-byte floating-point format into the program.

BSS.name: Block starting with symbol
BSS.summary: Leaves a gap of that many bytes for the program to use as working space. The label is the address of the first byte.

BES.name: Block ending with symbol
BES.summary: Leaves a gap of that many bytes. The label is the address just after the last byte.

EVEN.name: Even address
EVEN.summary: If the program has reached an odd address, skips one byte. Code and words must start on even addresses, so use it after BYTE or TEXT.

DEF.name: Define (make public)
DEF.summary: Tells the loader about a label, so it can be found by name. `DEF START` is what lets you type START as the program name.

REF.name: Reference (defined elsewhere)
REF.summary: Says these names are defined outside this program, usually helpers in the Editor/Assembler cartridge such as VSBW or KSCAN. The loader fills in their addresses.

AORG.name: Absolute origin
AORG.summary: Says exactly where in memory the following code must go, for example `AORG >A000` or `AORG >6000` for a cartridge.

RORG.name: Relocatable origin
RORG.summary: Goes back to code that the loader may place wherever there is room.

DORG.name: Dummy origin
DORG.summary: Lays out labels at an address without putting anything in the program. Handy for naming a block of working memory.

XORG.name: Execution origin (xas99)
XORG.summary: Says the following code will be copied to, and run from, a different address than where it sits in the program.

BANK.name: Bank (xas99)
BANK.summary: Starts a new bank of a bank-switched cartridge.

COPY.name: Copy in another file
COPY.summary: Pulls in another source file at this point, as if its lines were written here.

BCOPY.name: Copy in a binary file (xas99)
BCOPY.summary: Pulls in the raw bytes of another file at this point.

SAVE.name: Save range (xas99)
SAVE.summary: Says which range of addresses goes into the output file.

END.name: End of program
END.summary: Marks the end of the source. If a label follows, the program starts running there once it is loaded.

IDT.name: Program name
IDT.summary: Gives the program a name (up to 8 letters) inside the object file.

TITL.name: Listing title
TITL.summary: Sets the heading printed on the listing. Does not affect the program.

PAGE.name: Listing page break
PAGE.summary: Starts a new page in the listing. Does not affect the program.

LIST.name: Listing on
LIST.summary: Turns the listing back on. Does not affect the program.

UNL.name: Listing off
UNL.summary: Turns the listing off. Does not affect the program.

DXOP.name: Define extended operation
DXOP.summary: Gives a name to one of the XOP calls.

.IFDEF.name: If defined (xas99)
.IFDEF.summary: Only assemble the lines that follow (up to .else or .endif) if this name exists.

.IFNDEF.name: If not defined (xas99)
.IFNDEF.summary: Only assemble the lines that follow if this name does not exist.

.IFEQ.name: If equal (xas99)
.IFEQ.summary: Only assemble the lines that follow if the two values are equal (or the one value is 0).

.IFNE.name: If not equal (xas99)
.IFNE.summary: Only assemble the lines that follow if the two values are different (or the one value is not 0).

.IFGT.name: If greater (xas99)
.IFGT.summary: Only assemble the lines that follow if the first value is greater than the second.

.IFGE.name: If greater or equal (xas99)
.IFGE.summary: Only assemble the lines that follow if the first value is greater than or equal to the second.

.IFLT.name: If less (xas99)
.IFLT.summary: Only assemble the lines that follow if the first value is less than the second.

.IFLE.name: If less or equal (xas99)
.IFLE.summary: Only assemble the lines that follow if the first value is less than or equal to the second.

.ELSE.name: Otherwise (xas99)
.ELSE.summary: Starts the lines to assemble when the .if test was false.

.DEFM.name: Define macro (xas99)
.DEFM.summary: Starts a macro: a named group of lines you can reuse by writing .NAME. Inside it, #1, #2 ... stand for the values passed in.

.REPT.name: Repeat (xas99)
.REPT.summary: Repeats the lines up to .endr that many times.

.PRINT.name: Print a message (xas99)
.PRINT.summary: Shows a message while assembling. Does not affect the program.

.ERROR.name: Stop with an error (xas99)
.ERROR.summary: Stops assembling and shows a message.

symbols.VSBW:
**VSBW = VDP Single Byte Write.** An Editor/Assembler helper that writes one byte to video memory.

Video memory is the video chip's own 16K, where everything on screen lives. Your program can't write there directly, so it uses this helper.

R0 = where in video memory, left byte of R1 = the byte. Call with `BLWP @VSBW`.
symbols.VMBW:
**VMBW = VDP Multiple Byte Write.** An Editor/Assembler helper that copies a block of bytes into video memory.

Used for a line of text, character shapes or sprite patterns.

R0 = where in video memory, R1 = address of the bytes in your program, R2 = how many. Call with `BLWP @VMBW`.
symbols.VSBR:
**VSBR = VDP Single Byte Read.** An Editor/Assembler helper that reads one byte from video memory.

R0 = where in video memory. The byte comes back in the left byte of R1. Call with `BLWP @VSBR`.
symbols.VMBR:
**VMBR = VDP Multiple Byte Read.** An Editor/Assembler helper that copies a block of bytes out of video memory.

R0 = where in video memory, R1 = where to put them in your program, R2 = how many. Call with `BLWP @VMBR`.
symbols.VWTR:
**VWTR = VDP Write To Register.** An Editor/Assembler helper that changes one of the video chip's 8 settings (screen mode, colours, where tables are kept ...).

Left byte of R0 = which setting (0 to 7), right byte of R0 = the new value. Call with `BLWP @VWTR`.
symbols.KSCAN:
**KSCAN = Keyboard Scan.** An Editor/Assembler helper that checks the keyboard or a joystick once.

Put the mode in the byte at >8374 first (0 = whole keyboard, 1 and 2 = left/right half with joystick). The key code comes back in the byte at >8375 (>FF = none). Bit >20 of the byte at >837C is on when a new key was pressed. Call with `BLWP @KSCAN`.
symbols.GPLLNK:
**GPLLNK = GPL Link.** An Editor/Assembler helper that runs one of the console's built-in routines written in GPL (the TI's own internal language).

Call with `BLWP @GPLLNK` followed by a DATA line holding the routine's address.
symbols.XMLLNK:
**XMLLNK = XML Link.** An Editor/Assembler helper that runs one of the console's built-in machine-code routines (such as the floating-point maths).

Call with `BLWP @XMLLNK` followed by a DATA line saying which routine.
symbols.DSRLNK:
**DSRLNK = Device Service Routine Link.** An Editor/Assembler helper for talking to a device such as a disk drive, using a file description (PAB) kept in video memory.

Call with `BLWP @DSRLNK` followed by `DATA 8`.
symbols.LOADER:
**LOADER.** An Editor/Assembler helper that loads another object file from disk.

Call with `BLWP @LOADER`.

addresses.0000: The reset vector. `BLWP @>0000` restarts the console at the TI title screen.
addresses.6000: Start of the cartridge area (>6000 to >7FFF).
addresses.8300: Start of the fast RAM (256 bytes, >8300 to >83FF). Programs usually put their registers here with LWPI.
addresses.8370: Highest free address in video memory, kept by the console.
addresses.8374: Keyboard mode for KSCAN: 0 = whole keyboard, 1 = left half with joystick 1, 2 = right half with joystick 2.
addresses.8375: Key code from the last KSCAN (>FF = no key).
addresses.8376: Joystick up/down reading from the last KSCAN.
addresses.8377: Joystick left/right reading from the last KSCAN.
addresses.8378: Random number left by the console's RAND routine.
addresses.8379: Frame timer. The console's interrupt routine adds 1 to this byte every frame (while interrupts are on), so waiting for it to change waits for the next frame.
addresses.837A: Highest sprite number the console moves automatically.
addresses.837B: The console's copy of the video chip's status byte, taken once a frame by its interrupt routine.
addresses.837C: The console's status byte. Bit >20 is on when KSCAN found a new key.
addresses.83C2: Switches for the console's interrupt routine: bits here turn off its sprite motion, sound and QUIT key handling.
addresses.83C4: Address of your own once-a-frame routine. 0 = none. The console's interrupt routine calls it each frame.
addresses.83CC: Address of the sound list the console is playing.
addresses.83CE: Countdown for the console's sound list player. Set it to 1 to start a list.
addresses.83D4: The console's copy of video register 1. The console sends this back to the video chip after a key press, so set it to match your own register 1 value.
addresses.83D6: Screen blanking countdown. The console blanks the screen when it runs out; clear it to keep the screen on.
addresses.83E0: The console's own registers (>83E0 to >83FF). Its built-in routines use these, so keep your data out of here if you call them.
addresses.8400: The sound chip. Bytes written here set pitch and volume for its 3 tone voices and 1 noise voice.
addresses.8800: Video chip: read a data byte here.
addresses.8802: Video chip: read its status byte here. Reading it also clears the "new frame" flag.
addresses.8C00: Video chip: write a data byte here. The chip's address moves on by itself after each byte.
addresses.8C02: Video chip: write an address (two bytes, low byte first) or a register setting here.
addresses.9000: Speech synthesizer: read its status or a data byte here.
addresses.9400: Speech synthesizer: write commands and data here.
addresses.9800: GROM (the console's built-in program chips): read a data byte here.
addresses.9C00: GROM: write a data byte here.
addresses.9C02: GROM: write an address here (two bytes, high byte first).

sound._help: Turns on the sound player. A BYTE or DATA block marked '@sound' (or named like a sound) gets a Play link. The layout is the console's sound list: a count, that many bytes for the sound chip, then how long to wait in 60ths of a second; a count of 0 ends the list.
sound.about: The TI-99/4A's sound chip (the SN76489) has three tone voices and one noise voice. A sound list sends it bytes in steps: after each step the chip keeps sounding for the wait that was given.

sprites._help: Pictures kept as BYTE or DATA lines. Put a comment with @sprite (and a shape or size) just above the block to draw and edit it.
sprites.about: The TI-99/4A's video chip (the TMS9918A) draws characters and sprites from 8 bytes each, one byte a row, the left-most pixel in the top bit.

8x8.name: 8x8 character or sprite
8x8.about: 8 bytes, one a row, top row first.

16x16.name: 16x16 sprite
16x16.about: 32 bytes, as four 8x8 blocks: top-left, bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right. Switch on 16x16 sprites with bit 1 of video register 1.

snippets._help: Starter code. Type the name (in lower case) at the start of a line and pick it from the list, or run Retro ASM: Insert starter code. ${1:NAME} is a spot to fill in (Tab moves to the next one; the same number is filled in everywhere at once), $0 is where the cursor ends up.

program.name: A whole program to start from
program.about: The usual start and end of a TI-99/4A program loaded with Editor/Assembler (option 3). Your code goes in the middle. At the end it waits, so you can see what it did; FCTN = (QUIT) goes back to the title screen.
body: ; ${1:What this program does}
DEF  START           ; The loader looks for START
START  LWPI WRKSPC          ; Use our own 16 registers
LIMI 0               ; Turn off interrupts
STAY   LIMI 2               ; Let the console check FCTN = (QUIT)
LIMI 0
JMP  STAY            ; Wait here, so you can see what happened
; (To go straight back to the title screen instead: BLWP @>0000)
WRKSPC BSS  32              ; Room for R0-R15 (16 words)
END  START           ; The end; start running at START

routine.name: A routine called with BL
routine.about: A block of code you call with BL @NAME, which comes back with RT. If it calls another routine with BL itself, save R11 first, or the way back is lost.
body: ; ${1:NAME}: ${2:what it does}
; Call it with:  BL   @${1:NAME}
${1:NAME}
RT                   ; Back to the line after the BL

loop.name: Do something a number of times
loop.about: Counts a register down to 0, going round once for each count.
body: LI   R${1:1},${2:10}           ; How many times round
${3:LOOP}
DEC  R${1:1}              ; One fewer to go
JNE  ${3:LOOP}            ; Not 0 yet: go round again

vdpwrite.name: Write a byte to video memory
vdpwrite.about: Talks to the video chip directly: sends it an address, then the byte. Put a letter on the screen this way (address >0000 is the top-left corner).
body: ; Write one byte to video memory
LI   R0,${1:>0000}        ; Video address (>0000 is the top-left of the screen)
ORI  R0,>4000        ; Set the "write" bit
SWPB R0
MOVB R0,@>8C02       ; Send the address: right byte first ...
SWPB R0
MOVB R0,@>8C02       ; ... then the left byte
LI   R1,${2:>4100}        ; The byte goes in the left byte (>41 is "A")
MOVB R1,@>8C00       ; Write it

regions.text: the low part of the 32K memory expansion (8K of RAM)
plug-in card ROM (disk controller and the like)
a repeat of the fast RAM (the real one is at >8300 to >83FF)
the fast RAM (256 bytes inside the console)
the high part of the 32K memory expansion (24K of RAM)
